---

# Researching Portuguese Family History with Public, Authoritative Sources

**Research date:** 5 September 2026 · All findings below were verified by opening each site directly in the browser. Where a detail was not explicitly stated on the page, it is recorded as **"not stated."**

---

## Part 1 — Ranked List of Public Research Resources

### 🥇 1. DigitArq — DGLAB National Archives Portal (`digitarq.arquivos.pt`)
| Attribute | Verified finding |
|---|---|
| Custodian | Direção-Geral do Livro, dos Arquivos e das Bibliotecas (DGLAB) |
| Scale (site's own wording) | "more than 8 million contents… associated with more than 63 million images"; "more than 100 km of documents online" |
| Period/type | Parish registers, notarial, judicial, civil records; span varies by fonds |
| Images online | **Yes** — I opened a 30-image parish/testament book; full zoom, rotate and **download** worked with no account |
| Account/payment | **None.** Site states consultation is *"gratuitamente"* |
| Rights | Item viewed was licensed **CC BY-SA 4.0** |
| Geographic coverage | National — one search returned hits from Torre do Tombo (PT/TT), Arquivo Distrital de Viana do Castelo (PT/ADVCT) and Arquivo Distrital do Porto (PT/ADPRT) simultaneously |
| Searchability | Free-text search + advanced search; facets for **Documentos, Atores, Eventos, Lugares**; my test query returned 848 results |
| Source type | **Original records (digital images) + archival finding aid** |

**When to use:** Your first stop for almost any mainland enquiry. Because it searches many archives at once, it is the fastest way to discover that a book you want is held somewhere unexpected.

---

### 🥈 2. Registos Paroquiais e de Passaportes dos Açores (`culturacores.azores.gov.pt`)
Governo dos Açores – Secretaria Regional da Educação, Cultura e Desporto, Direção Regional da Cultura.

| Attribute | Verified finding |
|---|---|
| Period covered online | **1541 to 1911**, explicitly stated |
| Volume | **904,543 images/files online**, explicitly stated |
| Images online | **Yes** — I opened the Corvo baptisms 1900–1911 book; viewer with zoom/print, no login |
| Account/payment | **None** for viewing. Certificates must be requested from the three regional libraries/archives (e-mail addresses published) |
| Geographic coverage | All nine islands; originals held at Ponta Delgada (S. Miguel), Angra do Heroísmo (Terceira), Horta (Faial) |
| Searchability | Browse/filter by **Ilha → Concelho → Freguesia**, plus *Série*: Baptismos, Casamentos, Índices, Legitimações, Óbitos, Perfilhações, Reconhecimentos, **Róis/Confessados**, Tutelas. Navigation inside a book is by year → image number — **no personal-name index** |
| Source type | **Original records + genealogical inventory** ("Inventário Genealógico") |

**Why ranked so high:** It is the single most explicit public source I found about *how the Portuguese record system actually works* — see Part 2.

---

### 🥉 3. Arquivo Distrital de Braga / Universidade do Minho (`pesquisa.adb.uminho.pt`)
- A **cultural unit of the University of Minho**, holding regional archival responsibility for Braga district.
- **Founded 1917**; holds *"approximately five kilometres of documents produced over the last 12 centuries, including transcriptions of earlier documents dating back to the 6th century."*
- Free search; checkbox filter **"Only records with digital objects"**; advanced search; authority records for *Individual people* and *Collective people*.
- ⚠️ **Two caveats I verified directly:** (a) the site warns that much data came from *"older, non-standardized databases created using applications that did not support accents,"* and advises **searching using unaccented terms as well**; (b) the **Indexes** browse returned *"No records with associated indexing have been created yet."*

**When to use:** Essential for the Minho/Braga region, one of the richest ecclesiastical archives in Portugal (Braga was the primatial archdiocese).

---

### 4. Arquivo Nacional da Torre do Tombo (`antt.dglab.gov.pt`)
- A service of DGLAB under the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sport; one of the national-scope archives of the Portuguese archive network.
- Holds **original documents from the 9th century to the present day**.
- Access to its digitised material is delivered through DigitArq (#1).

**When to use:** For pre-parish-register and elite/institutional sources — Inquisition, Chancelarias, Habilitações, notarial and monastic fonds — that no district archive holds.

---

### 5. FamilySearch Research Wiki (`familysearch.org/en/wiki/...`)
Readable **without any login** (the record images are a separate matter). Licensed CC BY-SA; the Civil Registration page showed *last edited 15 January 2026*.

Verified statements from the **Portugal Civil Registration** page:
- **1832** — legislation required births, marriages and deaths to be recorded at a local civil registry; before this only churches recorded such information.
- Civil registers were first instituted for **non-Catholics**, with Catholic priests acting as civil registrar for their parish; *"the system didn't come into effect until 1878."*
- **From 1911 onward**, all residents were required to have vital events recorded with the civil registrar regardless of church registration.
- **Transfer rules to district archives:** births after **100 years**, marriages after **50 years**, deaths after **30 years**.
- Records under 100 years old are likely still at the Conservatória; *"due to privacy laws, you may need to prove your relationship."*
- *"Many times, Civil Registration records have not been digitized or microfilmed."*
- *"Most archives have a fee associated with locating and copying records."*

Also verified: the **Portuguese Genealogical Word List**, with a downloadable PDF and linked guides to Portuguese Handwriting (BYU Script Tutorial), Basic Portuguese Paleography, **Variations in Spelling**, Abbreviations, and Transcription of Characters.

**Source type: secondary / guidance** — excellent orientation, but always confirm against the archive itself.

---

### 6. Biblioteca Nacional Digital (`bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt`)
- Free, no login; English and Portuguese interfaces.
- Collections include **Cartografia**, Periódicos, Iconografia, Livros, Espólios, Códices Alcobacenses, Iluminados, Partituras.
- **Cartografia verified: 2,511 results**, with a rights facet showing **2,345 PUBLIC DOMAIN / 166 COPYRIGHTED**; date-range slider and faceted refinement.

**When to use:** Historical maps to resolve place-names and boundaries; printed *corografias*, local histories and periodicals for context.

---

### 7. Hemeroteca Digital, Câmara Municipal de Lisboa (`hemerotecadigital.cm-lisboa.pt`)
- Free, no login. Indexes by **Títulos, Autores, Cronológico, Geográfico, Géneros de Imprensa**.
- **Verified chronological coverage: 1715 → 1993**, and the index visibly shows **unlinked (non-digitised) years** — e.g. gaps around 1727, 1753, 1755, 1760, much of 1763–1774 and 1790–1809.

**When to use:** Obituaries, marriage notices, emigration/passenger notes, business and legal advertisements — the "connective tissue" between vital records.

---

### 8. Tombo.pt — independent parish-book index
⚠️ **Not an archive and not official.** Its About page states it is *"an individual initiative of the author, João Ventura, who doesn't work nor receives any support or privileged information from any of the Portuguese archives,"* and that he *"is unable to answer any questions about the future availability of the parish books, nor help in genealogical research."*

- **Free**, and states it *"will never restrict the access to information to subscribers"*; funded by sponsorship and **paid advertisements** (ads were visible on the page).
- Verified district book-counts, e.g. **Porto 40,688 · Bragança 36,307 · Guarda 33,247 · Lisboa 27,619 · Viseu 25,134 · Aveiro 22,650
